Part two. Fyre Festival. With only a few weeks left, they moved to a bare gravel lot. No water system. No toilets. No houses. Behind the scenes, money was running out. The villas were never built. Instead, they bought hundreds of disaster relief tents. April twenty seventh, twenty seventeen. The first planes landed. Wet mattresses. Piles of luggage dumped in the dark. Blink one eighty two had already pulled out. Then came the food. Two slices of bread, two slices of cheese, in a foam box. Within hours, the cheese sandwich went around the world. The next morning, the festival was cancelled. Local workers were left unpaid. One Bahamian restaurant owner, Maryann Rolle, used about fifty thousand dollars of her own savings to pay her staff. Billy pleaded guilty to fraud, and he was sentenced to six years in prison. Even a party that never existed can be sold with the perfect post.
